messages.subject: Re: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
messages.subject_clean: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yang,
I figured out the previous issues.

We are now interested in an enhancer region of about 4 kb. I have partitioned it into adjacent intervals (of 100 or 50 bp), created two annotation files for the intervals, one for the positive strand and the other for the negative strand, and ran these through featureCounts. Plotting the count distribution across intervals shows a strong peak for the negative strand, while there is nothing for the positive strand (this makes some sense biologically). Then I computed read counts at the single base level using samtools, also separately for the negative and the positive strand. I eliminated all multi-mapping reads before counting. However, the base count distribution shows peaks on both the negative and the positive strand (does not make much sense biologically). So I assume that featureCounts eliminates these reads on the positive strand. I think I need to do the base counting as close as possible to the way featureCounts performs the counting. Do you have any suggestions, does featureCounts filter reads based on mapping quality before counting? I run featureCounts with allowMultiOverlap=TRUE, minOverlap=1 and largestOverlap=TRUE.

Thank you once again, Ina

messages.subject_clean: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ina,

If your reads are paired-end, the second read nearly always has an opposite strandness to the first read. If you turned on the paired-end mode in featureCounts, the second read is flipped to the opposite strand before strand-specific read assignment. Maybe this can explain the difference between the results from featureCounts and samtools.

Cheers,
Yang

messages.subject: Re: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
messages.subject_clean: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
messages.body_plain:
Yes, you can define base positions as features in the SAF file. You may give all the features the same "gene name" or different "gene names" like

foo chr1 10000 10000 +
foo chr1 10001 10001 +
foo chr1 10002 10002 +
foo chr1 10003 10003 +
foo chr1 10004 10004 +
...
foo chr1 19999 19999 +
foo chr1 20000 20000 +

You then need to run featureCounts on the feature-level mode  (useMetaFeatures=FALSE) and allow multi-assignment of the reads (allowMultiOverlap = TRUE). This will give the number of reads mapped to each base location (ie, reads that have any mapped base at this base location) in your SAF file.

messages.subject_clean: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
messages.body_plain:
If you're doing single-base level read assignment, setting "largestOverlap=TRUE" is meaningless because all overlapping length is 1 bp between the read and each 1-bp "feature". It is suggested not using this parameter for single-base level read assignment because it makes the program slower.

The default value for "minOverlap" is 1.
